plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests three distinct design strategies for a dual-stopband bandpass filter: (1) UV-centered quarter-wave stacks prioritizing 355-365 nm suppression, (2) visible-centered stacks prioritizing 420-700 nm transmission, and (3) balanced dual-stopband stacks trading between both stopbands. All routes use the same Ta2O5/SiO2 material system and 36-layer maximum, but explore different thickness distribution hypotheses. Literature L01 directly supports the Ta2O5/SiO2 photonic crystal approach; L21 and L28 inform manufacturing considerations for this material pair. The key trade-off is stopband depth versus passband flatness - routes that disagree on which wavelength to center the quarter-wave condition will reveal where the performance boundary lies.

routes.title: UV-Centered Quarter-Wave Stack for Maximum Excitation Suppression
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A quarter-wave stack centered at 355 nm will achieve deeper UV stopband suppression than visible-centered designs, but at the cost of increased passband ripple in the 420-700 nm region.
routes.design_principle: Bragg reflection condition: alternating high/low index layers with optical thickness λ/4 at the target stopband wavelength creates constructive interference for reflection. Centering at 355 nm maximizes reflectance at the excitation wavelength.
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 36 layers, initialized near 355 nm quarter-wave condition (Ta2O5 ~62 nm, SiO2 ~95 nm), tuned during optimization
soft_objectives: keep individual layer thicknesses within 20-350 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Ta2O5/SiO2 material pair has known thermal stress behavior per L28
ion beam sputtering deposition recommended per L21
theory_basis: Quarter-wave Bragg stack theory for high-reflectance mirrors
Photonic crystal bandgap formation in 1D periodic structures
expected_advantages: Strongest UV stopband suppression among the three routes
known_risks: Visible passband may show significant ripple due to stopband edges
NIR stopband at 1030-1080 nm may be weaker as it relies on higher-order reflection
36 layers may increase thermal stress per L28
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 36-layer periodic dielectric filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees, unpolarized light. Stack structure: Air | (Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Gao)) repeated 18 times | Fused Silica. Initialize layer thicknesses near quarter-wave condition at 355 nm (Ta2O5 (Gao) approximately 62 nm, SiO2 (Gao) approximately 95 nm based on typical refractive indices). Optimize all 36 individual layer thicknesses within 20-350 nm bounds to minimize average transmittance in 355-365 nm and 1030-1080 nm bands while maximizing average transmittance in 420-700 nm band. Report final layer thickness sequence and transmittance spectra across 350-1100 nm.

routes.title: Visible-Centered Stack for Maximum Passband Transmission
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A quarter-wave stack centered at 550 nm (visible band center) will achieve higher and flatter transmission in 420-700 nm than UV-centered designs, but UV and NIR stopband suppression will be weaker.
routes.design_principle: Centering the Bragg condition at the passband center wavelength minimizes passband ripple by placing stopband edges symmetrically around the transmission window. This prioritizes signal collection over excitation suppression.
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 36 layers, initialized near 550 nm quarter-wave condition (Ta2O5 ~96 nm, SiO2 ~147 nm), tuned during optimization
soft_objectives: keep individual layer thicknesses within 20-350 nm
manufacturing_considerations: thicker layers may reduce deposition time variation sensitivity
Ta2O5/SiO2 interface quality critical per L21
theory_basis: Bandpass filter design via symmetric stopband placement
expected_advantages: Highest visible passband transmission among the three routes
Flatter passband response for consistent fluorescence collection
Thicker layers may be more manufacturable
known_risks: UV stopband at 355-365 nm may be insufficient for excitation suppression
NIR stopband may fall outside effective reflection band
May require more layers to achieve equivalent stopband depth
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 36-layer periodic dielectric filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees, unpolarized light. Stack structure: Air | (Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Gao)) repeated 18 times | Fused Silica. Initialize layer thicknesses near quarter-wave condition at 550 nm (Ta2O5 (Gao) approximately 96 nm, SiO2 (Gao) approximately 147 nm based on typical refractive indices). Optimize all 36 individual layer thicknesses within 20-350 nm bounds to maximize average transmittance in 420-700 nm while minimizing average transmittance in 355-365 nm and 1030-1080 nm bands. Report final layer thickness sequence and transmittance spectra across 350-1100 nm.

routes.title: Dual-Stopband Balanced Stack with Mixed Quarter-Wave Conditions
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A non-periodic stack with layer thicknesses optimized for both 355 nm and 1050 nm quarter-wave conditions simultaneously will achieve acceptable suppression in both stopbands while maintaining reasonable visible transmission.
routes.design_principle: By varying layer thicknesses within the stack (some layers near 355 nm quarter-wave, others near 1050 nm quarter-wave), multiple reflection bands can be created. This sacrifices peak performance in any single band for balanced dual-stopband performance.

design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 36 layers, initialized with mixed pattern: odd pairs near 355 nm quarter-wave, even pairs near 1050 nm quarter-wave, tuned during optimization
soft_objectives: balance average transmittance minimization in 355-365 nm and 1030-1080 nm
maintain average transmittance above threshold in 420-700 nm
keep individual layer thicknesses within 20-350 nm
manufacturing_considerations: thickness variation between adjacent layers may increase deposition complexity
thermal stress management critical per L28 with mixed thickness pattern
L01 supports Ta2O5/SiO2 for photonic crystal applications
theory_basis: Multi-band photonic crystal design via thickness modulation
Superposition of multiple Bragg reflection conditions
expected_advantages: More flexible design space than periodic stacks
May reveal optimal trade-off point between competing objectives
known_risks: Neither stopband may achieve deep suppression compared to single-band optimized designs
Passband ripple may be irregular due to non-periodic structure
Optimization landscape may be more complex with multiple local minima
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 36-layer custom dielectric filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees, unpolarized light. Stack structure: Air | alternating Ta2O5 (Gao) and SiO2 (Gao) layers (36 total layers, 18 of each material) | Fused Silica. Initialize layer thicknesses with mixed pattern: layers 1-18 near 355 nm quarter-wave condition, layers 19-36 near 1050 nm quarter-wave condition. Optimize all 36 individual layer thicknesses within 20-350 nm bounds to balance minimization of average transmittance in 355-365 nm and 1030-1080 nm bands while maintaining high average transmittance in 420-700 nm band. Report final layer thickness sequence and transmittance spectra across 350-1100 nm.

routes.title: 36-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 dual-stopband Bragg stack with thickness optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 36-layer alternating high-low index stack with independently tunable layer thicknesses can achieve simultaneous suppression at 355-365 nm and 1030-1080 nm while maintaining transmittance above 80% in 420-700 nm, by exploiting the natural harmonic relationship between quarter-wave stack reflection bands.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg stacks produce high reflectance at the design wavelength and its harmonics. By optimizing individual layer thicknesses rather than fixing them at quarter-wave values, the stack can be tuned to create two distinct stopbands at non-harmonically-related wavelengths while keeping the intermediate visible region as a passband. The large index contrast between Ta2O5 (n~2.1-2.3) and SiO2 (n~1.45-1.47) provides strong reflection per pair, reducing the number of layers needed for deep stopbands.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 36 layers, each bounded 20-350 nm
manufacturing_considerations: all layer thicknesses must remain within 20-350 nm range for deposition feasibility
36 layers is at the upper limit of the constraint, which may increase deposition time and stress
Ta2O5 and SiO2 are standard e-beam or sputter deposition materials with well-known process control
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness (n×d = λ/4) produces maximum reflectance at the design wavelength for a Bragg stack
Higher index contrast between alternating layers increases reflectance per pair and widens the stopband
Bragg stacks naturally produce reflection harmonics at odd multiples of the fundamental design wavelength
Visible passband between two stopbands requires careful thickness tuning to avoid unintended reflection peaks in the 420-700 nm range
36 layers (18 pairs) should provide sufficient optical density for >OD3 suppression in both stopbands if optimized correctly
Layer thickness optimization can shift stopband centers away from natural harmonic positions
expected_advantages: Maximum degrees of freedom with 36 independent thickness variables allows fine-tuning of both stopband positions
Alternating high-low structure is manufacturable with standard deposition tools
Ta2O5/SiO2 pair has low absorption in visible and UV, minimizing passband loss
Symmetric topology simplifies optimization convergence compared to aperiodic sequences
known_risks: Ta2O5 is not in the guaranteed_names list; local resolution must confirm it maps to exactly one dataset - if it matches multiple stoichiometries, the route will be rejected and needs a specific measurement name

Refractive index values for Ta2O5 and SiO2 at 355 nm, 1050 nm, and across 420-700 nm are recalled from memory and may differ from the actual catalog data - absorption (k) in Ta2O5 at 355 nm could be higher than expected

The natural harmonic relationship of Bragg stacks may make it difficult to place stopbands at 360 nm and 1050 nm simultaneously without creating unwanted reflection in the visible passband - this may require more than 36 layers for adequate suppression

Quarter-wave thickness for 1050 nm NIR band requires ~125 nm Ta2O5 and ~180 nm SiO2, which is within the 20-350 nm constraint but leaves less room for UV band layers which need ~40 nm and ~60 nm - the wide thickness range may challenge optimization convergence
No literature was checked on dual-band filter design strategies; a chirped or apodized design might outperform this simple alternating approach but was not explored
The hypothesis that 36 layers is sufficient for dual stopbands is unverified - if suppression is inadequate, the constraint itself may need relaxation
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 36-layer planar dielectric filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees, unpolarized light. Materials are Ta2O5 (Gao) and SiO2 (Gao) in alternating order starting with Ta2O5 (Gao) at the air side. All 36 layer thicknesses are independent optimization variables bounded between 20 nm and 350 nm. Minimize average transmittance in the 355-365 nm band, minimize average transmittance in the 1030-1080 nm band, minimize transmittance at 355 nm, and maximize average transmittance in the 420-700 nm band. Report the optimized thicknesses for all 36 layers, the transmittance spectrum from 350 nm to 1100 nm, and the average transmittance in each target band. Compare the trade-off between passband transmittance and stopband suppression across optimization iterations.

research_influence: L01 directly supports the Ta2O5/SiO2 material pair choice for 1D photonic crystal structures, cited in all three routes for material system justification
L21 informs manufacturing considerations for Ta2O5/SiO2 ion beam sputtered coatings, cited in route_01 and route_02 for deposition method guidance
L28 warns about thermal stress in Ta2O5/SiO2 multilayer coatings, cited in all routes for manufacturing risk awareness
L29 discusses absorption in amorphous Ta2O5 and SiO2 films, cited in route_02 and route_03 for material loss considerations
unresolved_decisions: ta2o5 is not in guaranteed_names and will require local registry resolution before execution - if it resolves to multiple datasets, the route must specify which measurement set to use
The exact refractive index values at 355 nm, 550 nm, and 1050 nm will be read from resolved material datasets, not assumed in planning
Final layer count (36 vs. fewer) may be adjusted during optimization if performance saturates before reaching maximum layers
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all three routes fail to achieve acceptable dual-stopband suppression with reasonable visible transmission, the fundamental constraint may be the 36-layer limit or the Ta2O5/SiO2 material pair - consider requesting additional layers or alternative high-index materials in a follow-up study.

errors: This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone. No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied -- neither for the initial plan nor for any continuation round. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.

catalog.coverage: the guaranteed-name list proves name resolution only; the separate route candidate ranking reads actual n/k grids and records native coverage or explicit interpolation/endpoint-extension availability. Execution still keeps the registry's allow_extrapolation switch fail-closed
catalog.source: tmm_engine.MaterialRegistry local provider, each name resolved before listing

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a 36-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 Bragg stack with independently optimized layer thicknesses can simultaneously suppress two distant stopbands (355-365 nm UV and 1030-1080 nm NIR) while maintaining high transmittance in the visible passband (420-700 nm). The design draws on recalled knowledge of quarter-wave stack physics, harmonic reflection bands, and the trade-off between stopband width and pair count. No literature was consulted; all design choices are from prior knowledge of thin-film optics principles.

routes.title: 36-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 dual-stopband Bragg stack with thickness optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 36-layer alternating high-low index stack with independently tunable layer thicknesses can achieve simultaneous suppression at 355-365 nm and 1030-1080 nm while maintaining transmittance above 80% in 420-700 nm, by exploiting the natural harmonic relationship between quarter-wave stack reflection bands.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg stacks produce high reflectance at the design wavelength and its harmonics. By optimizing individual layer thicknesses rather than fixing them at quarter-wave values, the stack can be tuned to create two distinct stopbands at non-harmonically-related wavelengths while keeping the intermediate visible region as a passband. The large index contrast between Ta2O5 (n~2.1-2.3) and SiO2 (n~1.45-1.47) provides strong reflection per pair, reducing the number of layers needed for deep stopbands.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 36 layers, each bounded 20-350 nm
manufacturing_considerations: all layer thicknesses must remain within 20-350 nm range for deposition feasibility
36 layers is at the upper limit of the constraint, which may increase deposition time and stress
Ta2O5 and SiO2 are standard e-beam or sputter deposition materials with well-known process control
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness (n×d = λ/4) produces maximum reflectance at the design wavelength for a Bragg stack
Higher index contrast between alternating layers increases reflectance per pair and widens the stopband
Bragg stacks naturally produce reflection harmonics at odd multiples of the fundamental design wavelength
Visible passband between two stopbands requires careful thickness tuning to avoid unintended reflection peaks in the 420-700 nm range
36 layers (18 pairs) should provide sufficient optical density for >OD3 suppression in both stopbands if optimized correctly
Layer thickness optimization can shift stopband centers away from natural harmonic positions
expected_advantages: Maximum degrees of freedom with 36 independent thickness variables allows fine-tuning of both stopband positions
Alternating high-low structure is manufacturable with standard deposition tools
Ta2O5/SiO2 pair has low absorption in visible and UV, minimizing passband loss
Symmetric topology simplifies optimization convergence compared to aperiodic sequences
known_risks: Ta2O5 is not in the guaranteed_names list; local resolution must confirm it maps to exactly one dataset - if it matches multiple stoichiometries, the route will be rejected and needs a specific measurement name

Refractive index values for Ta2O5 and SiO2 at 355 nm, 1050 nm, and across 420-700 nm are recalled from memory and may differ from the actual catalog data - absorption (k) in Ta2O5 at 355 nm could be higher than expected

The natural harmonic relationship of Bragg stacks may make it difficult to place stopbands at 360 nm and 1050 nm simultaneously without creating unwanted reflection in the visible passband - this may require more than 36 layers for adequate suppression

Quarter-wave thickness for 1050 nm NIR band requires ~125 nm Ta2O5 and ~180 nm SiO2, which is within the 20-350 nm constraint but leaves less room for UV band layers which need ~40 nm and ~60 nm - the wide thickness range may challenge optimization convergence
No literature was checked on dual-band filter design strategies; a chirped or apodized design might outperform this simple alternating approach but was not explored
The hypothesis that 36 layers is sufficient for dual stopbands is unverified - if suppression is inadequate, the constraint itself may need relaxation
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 36-layer planar dielectric filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees, unpolarized light. Materials are Ta2O5 (Gao) and SiO2 (Gao) in alternating order starting with Ta2O5 (Gao) at the air side. All 36 layer thicknesses are independent optimization variables bounded between 20 nm and 350 nm. Minimize average transmittance in the 355-365 nm band, minimize average transmittance in the 1030-1080 nm band, minimize transmittance at 355 nm, and maximize average transmittance in the 420-700 nm band. Report the optimized thicknesses for all 36 layers, the transmittance spectrum from 350 nm to 1100 nm, and the average transmittance in each target band. Compare the trade-off between passband transmittance and stopband suppression across optimization iterations.
